newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Heavy ship workers begin strike.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Heavy ship workers begin strike.

text.p: Union workers at South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries, the nation's biggest shipbuilder, launched a strike on Thursday in protest at a new national labour law, a union official said.
An official at the company's public relations department said: "More and more workers are leaving their jobs to gather for a rally called by the labour union".
A union official at the main shipyard of Daewoo Heavy Industries said workers there had decided to go on strike from 8.00 a.m. on Friday (2300 GMT Thursday).
Earlier, a union body representing six leading shipyards said strikes would begin at 1.00 p.m. (0400 GMT).

The other four yards belong to Hyundai Mipo Dockyards, Halla Heavy Industries, Hanjin Heavy Industries and Korea Tacoma. It was not immediately clear if workers at those yards had actually walked out.
